question: What is the primary purpose of decontamination in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To ensure that expired drugs are safely disposed of in the incinerator
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new medical instruments
options.C: To make hospital wards smell fresh and clean for visitors
options.D: To break the chain of infection and protect patients and staff

explanation: Decontamination removes or destroys harmful microorganisms to stop them from spreading to vulnerable patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why are patients with surgical wounds or catheters at higher risk if equipment is poorly decontaminated?

options.A: They usually stay in the hospital longer than other patients do
options.B: They produce more body heat which helps bacteria multiply faster
options.C: Their immune systems completely stop working during recovery
options.D: Their natural body barriers are breached, allowing germs to enter easily

explanation: Surgical wounds and catheters bypass the body's normal physical defenses, providing a direct entry point for pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which decontamination process is required to completely destroy bacterial spores?
explanation: Only sterilization is powerful enough to destroy all microbial life, including tough bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why must an instrument be thoroughly cleaned before it undergoes disinfection or sterilization?

options.A: Cleaning agents instantly sterilize the instrument without needing an autoclave
options.B: Leftover organic matter and dirt can shield germs from the chemical or heat
options.C: Dry blood makes the metal instruments much heavier to carry
options.D: Patients will complain if the instruments look dull or stained

explanation: Organic debris like blood and tissue acts as a physical barrier that prevents disinfectants and steam from reaching the microorganisms underneath. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: According to the Spaulding classification, what level of processing is required for surgical instruments?
explanation: Surgical instruments are classified as critical items because they enter sterile tissues, so they must be fully sterilized. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to use a blood pressure cuff on a patient with unbroken skin. How should this item be classified and processed?

options.A: Semi-critical item requiring high-level chemical disinfection
options.B: Critical item requiring high-pressure steam sterilization
options.C: Non-critical item requiring low to intermediate-level disinfection
options.D: Sterile item requiring single-use disposal packaging

explanation: Blood pressure cuffs touch only intact skin, making them non-critical items that only need routine low or intermediate disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a hospital?
explanation: Washing hands or using alcohol-based hand rub is universally recognized as the most effective action to stop infection transmission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why do standard precautions apply to every single patient in the ward, even those not diagnosed with an infection?

options.A: Patients get offended if healthcare workers wear gloves only for some beds
options.B: Some patients may carry infections without showing any symptoms yet
options.C: Hospital management requires it only for statistical record keeping
options.D: It is too difficult for nurses to remember different rules for different people

explanation: Standard precautions assume any body fluid can carry pathogens because asymptomatic carriers can transmit infections unknowingly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take with a surgical instrument immediately after a procedure is finished?

options.A: Wrap it tightly in sterile cloth for storage
options.B: Soak the instrument in strong bleach overnight
options.C: Place it directly into the clean instrument cabinet
options.D: Remove gross soil and blood to prevent drying

explanation: Wiping off heavy blood and tissue right away keeps it from drying onto the metal, which makes later cleaning much harder. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Where should sterilized instruments be kept after they have been processed and wrapped?

options.A: Directly on the floor of the utility room
options.B: Inside a warm, humid washing sink basin
options.C: On an open counter in the busy main hallway
options.D: In a clean, dry, and dust-free storage area

explanation: Proper storage protects sterilized packs from moisture, dust, and contamination until they are needed for the next patient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is it a mistake to wipe a chemical disinfectant off a surface immediately after spraying it?

options.A: Leaving it wet makes the table look shiny and polished to visitors
options.B: The chemical needs a specific contact time to successfully kill the germs
options.C: The cleaning cloth will instantly dissolve if it touches wet disinfectant
options.D: Quick drying causes the chemical to release poisonous gases into the room

explanation: Disinfectants require time to act against pathogens; wiping them away prematurely prevents complete disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which chemical compound is commonly used for disinfecting blood spills on hard surfaces due to its quick action and low cost?
explanation: Sodium hypochlorite, commonly known as bleach, is an affordable and effective disinfectant for clearing up blood spills. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which specific vaccination is especially critical for healthcare workers who handle decontamination and sharps?
explanation: The Hepatitis B vaccine is essential for protecting staff against bloodborne pathogen exposure from contaminated instruments and needles. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: What type of protective equipment is recommended when working with harsh chemical disinfectants that might splash?

options.A: Paper surgical caps and cloth masks
options.B: Open sandals and thin cotton gowns

explanation: Face shields protect the eyes and mucous membranes from chemical splashes, while waterproof aprons protect clothing and skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: Where should used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades be disposed of immediately after use?
explanation: Sharps must always go into dedicated, puncture-proof safety containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)

question: Why is waste segregation at the point of generation considered so important in healthcare facilities?

options.A: It reduces the physical weight of general rubbish bins
options.B: It allows the hospital to recycle all medical waste into children's toys
options.C: It ensures hazardous infectious waste is treated correctly before final disposal
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for cleaning hospital floors

explanation: Separating waste immediately prevents infectious materials from mixing with ordinary household rubbish, protecting everyone from accidental contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)
